lessons.title: Outils d'artiste professionnel
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore and safely use professional art tools

mindsOn.activity: Mystery tool exploration: Show professional art tools (palette knives, brayers, fine brushes, sculpting tools) in covered containers. Students guess what each tool does. Introduce vocabulary: OUTIL (show tool gesture), PROFESSIONNEL (formal, careful handling), SÉCURITÉ (safe handling demonstration).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Real professional art tools, safety demonstration pictures, vocabulary cards with tool images
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students are overwhelmed by tool complexity: Start with just 2-3 tools and focus on safety. If they're very interested: Allow more exploration time and tool comparison.

activities: Tool Safety Training (~8 min): Learn proper handling for each professional tool. Practice safe passing, storage, and cleaning. Role-play being 'professional artists' with responsible tool use. Say 'Je suis sécuritaire avec mes outils!'

Tool Exploration Stations (~15 min): Rotate through stations with different professional tools. Try palette knife painting, brayer printing, fine detail brushwork, sculpting tool texture-making. Practice vocabulary at each station.
Tool Matching Challenge (~4 min): Match tools to their best uses. Discussion: 'Quel outil pour quel travail?' Practice professional vocabulary while explaining tool choices.
materials: Professional art tools (palette knives, brayers, detail brushes, sculpting tools)
action.visualSupport: Tool safety demonstration cards, tool-to-task matching visuals, professional artist photos using tools
action.decisionPoint: If tools are too advanced: Simplify to more basic versions but maintain professional vocabulary. If students master quickly: Introduce more specialized tools.

consolidation.activity: Professional Artist Role-Play. Students choose their favorite professional tool and demonstrate proper use to 'art students' (classmates). Practice vocabulary: 'Cet outil professionnel fait...' Emphasize safety and skill.
consolidation.assessment: Can students handle professional tools safely? Do they use tool vocabulary appropriately? Can they explain why professional tools require special care?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students struggle with safety: Extend safety practice before using tools independently. If they're very responsible: Plan more advanced tool introduction for future lessons.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Tool study without handling: Use pictures and videos of professional artists using tools, practice vocabulary and safety concepts without physical tool use.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that artists use special tools, like how doctors, builders, or chefs have professional tools

lessons.title: Mélange des médiums
lessons.oneGoal: Students will combine different art materials in single artworks

mindsOn.activity: Show examples of mixed media artworks. Identify different materials used together: paint + collage, crayon + watercolor, etc. Introduce vocabulary: MÉLANGER (mixing gesture), MÉDIUM (hold up different materials), COMBINAISON (bringing hands together).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Mixed media artwork examples, separate art materials, combination demonstration cards
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students are confused by multiple materials: Start with just two materials to combine. If they understand quickly: Show more complex mixed media examples.

activities: Media Experimentation (~10 min): Try simple combinations: crayon resist with watercolor, collage with paint details, chalk pastels with markers. Say 'Je mélange deux médiums!' Observe how materials interact.
Combination Planning (~8 min): Choose 3 different art materials. Plan artwork that uses all three meaningfully. Sketch plan showing where each medium will be used. Practice vocabulary while planning.
Mixed Media Creation (~9 min): Create planned mixed media artwork. Focus on how different mediums can enhance each other. Document process: 'D'abord crayon, puis peinture, enfin collage!'
materials: Variety of art materials (paints, crayons, markers, collage materials, pastels)
action.visualSupport: Step-by-step mixed media process cards, successful combination examples, planning templates
action.decisionPoint: If combinations aren't working: Provide tested successful combinations to try. If students are very experimental: Allow complete freedom in material combinations.

consolidation.activity: Mixed Media Gallery Walk. Display all mixed media works. Students identify different mediums used in each artwork. Practice vocabulary: 'Je vois une combinaison de...' Discuss which combinations were most effective.
consolidation.assessment: Can students successfully combine different art materials? Do they use mixed media vocabulary appropriately? Can they plan intentional combinations rather than random mixing?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students want to continue experimenting: Set up mixed media exploration station for future work. If they're satisfied with results: focus on analyzing successful combinations.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Mixed media planning: Use magazines and art materials to plan mixed media combinations without creating full artworks, focusing on vocabulary and combination concepts.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Mixing different ingredients in cooking, combining different materials in building projects

lessons.title: Techniques de peinture avancées
lessons.oneGoal: Students will master advanced painting techniques beyond basic brushwork

mindsOn.activity: Compare basic brush painting to advanced techniques using demonstrations. Show sponge painting, stencil work, palette knife techniques. Introduce vocabulary: TECHNIQUE (skillful gesture), ÉPONGE (dabbing motion), POCHOIR (stencil demonstration).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Side-by-side comparison of basic vs advanced painting techniques, tools for each technique
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle with basic brushwork: Review brush basics before advancing. If they're ready for challenge: demonstrate more complex advanced techniques.

activities: Sponge Technique Mastery (~9 min): Learn controlled sponge painting for textures and effects. Practice dabbing, stippling, gradient creation. Say 'Ma technique d'éponge crée...' Compare to brush effects.

Stencil Precision Work (~9 min): Use stencils (premade and self-cut) for clean, precise designs. Learn proper stencil holding, paint application, clean removal. Practice 'technique de pochoir' vocabulary.

Palette Knife Exploration (~9 min): Use palette knives for paint application, texture creation, and mixing. Practice controlled spreading, scraping, and detail work. Advanced tool from Lesson 1 applied to painting.
action.visualSupport: Technique demonstration cards, examples of each advanced technique, step-by-step process posters
action.decisionPoint: If techniques are too difficult: Simplify to one technique per lesson. If students master quickly: combine techniques in single artworks.

consolidation.activity: Technique Showcase. Students demonstrate their best advanced technique to classmates. Explain process: 'Ma technique avancée utilise...' Compare effects achieved with different techniques.
consolidation.assessment: Can students execute advanced painting techniques with control? Do they use technique vocabulary accurately? Can they choose appropriate techniques for desired effects?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students need more practice: plan additional technique refinement sessions. If they've mastered techniques: challenge them to invent new techniques.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Technique analysis: Study photos and videos of advanced painting techniques, practice vocabulary and technique identification without hands-on painting.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Watching house painters use different techniques, seeing how artists create different effects

lessons.title: Sculpture et modelage
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create three-dimensional artworks using various sculpting materials

mindsOn.activity: Explore 3D vs 2D concepts using simple objects and pictures. Handle sculptures vs looking at paintings. Introduce vocabulary: SCULPTURE (3D gesture with hands), MODELAGE (shaping clay motion), FORME (outline 3D shapes in air).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Real sculpture examples, 2D/3D comparison objects, sculpting tools and materials
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle with 3D concept: Use more concrete examples and manipulation activities. If they understand quickly: introduce more complex sculptural concepts.

activities: Clay Exploration (~10 min): Learn basic clay techniques: pinching, coiling, slab building. Practice vocabulary: 'Je fais du modelage!' Focus on 3D thinking rather than flat shapes.

Additive Sculpture (~8 min): Build sculptures by adding materials together (clay pieces, found objects, natural materials). Practice 'construction de sculpture' vocabulary. Think about all sides of artwork.
Subtractive Carving (~9 min): Remove material to create forms (soft carving materials like soap, foam). Practice controlled removal. Say 'J'enlève pour créer ma forme!' Compare to additive process.
action.visualSupport: 3D process demonstration cards, additive vs subtractive examples, sculptural vocabulary posters
action.decisionPoint: If fine motor skills are challenging: Focus on larger, simpler forms. If students excel: introduce more detailed sculptural techniques.

consolidation.activity: Sculpture Gallery. Display 3D works so they can be viewed from all angles. Students walk around sculptures, describing what they see from different viewpoints. Practice 3D vocabulary.
consolidation.assessment: Can students think and work three-dimensionally? Do they use sculpture vocabulary appropriately? Can they plan and execute basic sculptural techniques?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If sculptures need more work time: plan extended sculpture sessions. If students are satisfied: focus on presentation and 3D analysis skills.

lessons.emergencyBackup: 3D construction with classroom materials: Use blocks, boxes, and other classroom items to explore 3D construction concepts and practice vocabulary.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing with playdough, building with blocks, shaping sand castles

lessons.title: Gravure et impression
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create multiple copies of artworks using printmaking techniques

mindsOn.activity: Demonstrate concept of making multiple copies: stamp a simple design multiple times. Compare to unique artworks vs prints. Introduce vocabulary: GRAVURE (carving motion), IMPRESSION (printing press motion), MULTIPLES (counting copies).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of original artworks vs prints, simple stamping demonstration, professional printmaking examples
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students don't understand multiples concept: Use more concrete examples like photocopies or stamps. If they understand: show more sophisticated printmaking examples.

activities: Simple Relief Printing (~10 min): Create printing blocks using foam plates, cardboard, or potatoes. Carve/cut designs, apply paint, make multiple prints. Practice 'faire une gravure' vocabulary.
Monoprinting Exploration (~8 min): Create one-of-a-kind prints using paint on plastic, then transferring to paper. Compare to multiple prints. Practice impression vocabulary.
Print Series Creation (~9 min): Make series of 3-5 identical prints using relief method. Number prints: 'Impression numéro un, deux, trois...' Understand concept of edition.
materials: Printmaking materials (foam plates, cardboard, cutting tools)
action.visualSupport: Printmaking process demonstration, examples of print series, professional printmaker tools
action.decisionPoint: If printing is too complex: Focus on simple stamping and multiples concept. If students love printmaking: introduce more sophisticated techniques.

consolidation.activity: Print Exhibition and Trading. Display print series. Students can trade prints with each other since multiple copies exist. Discuss how printmaking allows sharing artwork. Practice printmaking vocabulary.
consolidation.assessment: Can students create multiple identical prints? Do they understand printmaking vocabulary? Can they plan designs that work well for printing?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If prints are very successful: plan more advanced printmaking sessions. If technique was challenging: review simpler printing methods.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Print analysis and planning: Study different types of prints, plan printmaking designs on paper, practice vocabulary without actual printing process.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Stamps, copying machines, printed books and newspapers

lessons.title: Collage sophistiqué
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create complex collages using advanced layering and composition

mindsOn.activity: Compare simple collages to sophisticated examples. Identify layers, composition principles, intentional material choices. Introduce vocabulary: COLLAGE (layering gesture), COUCHE (layer-building motion), COMPOSITION (arranging gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Simple vs sophisticated collage examples, layering demonstration, composition principle visuals
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students need collage basics review: spend time on fundamental cutting and pasting. If they're ready for complexity: focus on advanced composition concepts.

activities: Advanced Material Selection (~8 min): Choose collage materials intentionally for color, texture, meaning. Practice vocabulary: 'Je choisis ce matériel pour...' Consider how materials work together compositionally.

Complex Layering Techniques (~10 min): Create depth through layering: foreground, middle ground, background. Use transparency, overlap, scale changes. Practice 'couche' vocabulary while building layers.
Compositional Planning (~9 min): Plan overall composition considering balance, focal point, movement. Arrange before gluing. Practice 'composition' vocabulary while making decisions.
materials: Variety of sophisticated collage materials (textured papers, transparencies, fabrics)
action.visualSupport: Composition planning templates, layering technique examples, advanced collage artist examples
action.decisionPoint: If planning is too abstract: focus on hands-on exploration with guidance. If students excel at planning: introduce more complex compositional concepts.

consolidation.activity: Collage Critique Session. Students present their sophisticated collages, explaining layering and compositional choices. Use advanced vocabulary: 'Ma composition utilise des couches pour...'
consolidation.assessment: Can students create intentionally complex collages? Do they use advanced collage vocabulary meaningfully? Can they make sophisticated compositional decisions?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If collages need more work: provide additional studio time. If students are proud of results: plan exhibition or documentation of sophisticated work.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Collage analysis and planning: Study sophisticated collages in art books or online, plan complex collages on paper using drawing and vocabulary practice.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Magazine layouts, scrapbooks, mood boards, advertising design

lessons.title: Art textile
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore fiber arts including weaving, stitching, and fabric manipulation

mindsOn.activity: Explore different textiles: woven vs knitted vs sewn. Feel different fabric textures and structures. Introduce vocabulary: TEXTILE (fabric touching motion), TISSER (weaving motion with fingers), COUDRE (stitching motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Variety of textile examples showing different construction methods, textile tools, cultural textile examples
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students have limited textile experience: focus on simple fabric exploration and basic vocabulary. If they have textile knowledge: connect to cultural and historical contexts.

activities: Simple Weaving (~10 min): Use cardboard looms or simple frames to weave with yarn, fabric strips, or natural materials. Practice 'tisser' vocabulary. Over, under, over, under pattern.
Basic Stitching (~8 min): Learn simple running stitch to join fabrics or create decorative lines. Use large needles and felt or burlap. Practice 'coudre' vocabulary with safety.
Fabric Manipulation (~9 min): Experiment with pleating, gathering, fraying, layering fabrics for artistic effects. Create texture and dimension. Practice textile vocabulary while exploring.
materials: Simple weaving looms or cardboard frames
action.visualSupport: Weaving pattern diagrams, stitching technique cards, fabric manipulation examples
action.decisionPoint: If fine motor skills are challenging: focus on larger-scale textile work. If students enjoy precision work: introduce more detailed techniques.

consolidation.activity: Textile Arts Appreciation. Display textile creations and discuss how textile arts connect to clothing, decoration, and cultural traditions. Practice textile vocabulary in context.
consolidation.assessment: Can students execute basic textile techniques? Do they use textile vocabulary appropriately? Can they appreciate textile arts as legitimate art form?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students love textile work: plan more advanced fiber arts exploration. If they found it challenging: focus on appreciation and vocabulary rather than complex techniques.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Textile exploration without tools: Examine different fabrics and textiles, practice vocabulary, plan textile art projects using drawing and fabric samples.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Clothing construction, quilts, traditional crafts, home decoration

lessons.title: Techniques mixtes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will combine multiple advanced techniques in single complex artworks

mindsOn.activity: Review all advanced techniques learned in previous lessons. Show examples of artworks combining multiple techniques. Introduce vocabulary: MIXTE (combining gesture), COMPLEXE (layered complexity gesture), INTÉGRER (integration motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of multi-technique artworks, technique review cards from previous lessons, integration planning templates
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students need technique review: spend more time reconnecting with previous lessons. If they remember well: focus on integration planning.

activities: Technique Integration Planning (~8 min): Choose 3-4 advanced techniques to combine in one artwork. Plan how each technique will be used and how they'll work together. Practice 'intégrer' vocabulary.
Complex Artwork Creation (~15 min): Execute planned multi-technique artwork. May combine: advanced painting + printmaking + collage + textile elements. Focus on intentional integration.
Process Documentation (~4 min): Document creation process showing how multiple techniques were integrated. Practice vocabulary: 'J'ai intégré ces techniques mixtes pour...'
materials: All materials from previous advanced technique lessons
action.visualSupport: Integration planning templates, multi-technique process examples, technique combination charts
action.decisionPoint: If integration is overwhelming: limit to 2-3 techniques. If students excel: encourage experimentation with unconventional technique combinations.

consolidation.activity: Complex Artwork Presentation. Students present their multi-technique works, explaining how different techniques were integrated. Use sophisticated vocabulary to describe complex creative decisions.
consolidation.assessment: Can students successfully integrate multiple advanced techniques? Do they use complex art vocabulary meaningfully? Can they plan and execute sophisticated multi-technique works?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If artworks are very successful: plan advanced exhibition or documentation. If students struggled with integration: focus on simpler technique combinations.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Integration planning and analysis: Plan multi-technique artworks on paper, analyze complex artworks by other artists, practice integration vocabulary without full creation.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Professional artists combining many techniques, complex craft projects

lessons.title: Style personnel avancé
lessons.oneGoal: Students will develop and articulate their own advanced artistic style

mindsOn.activity: Look at students' artwork from throughout the unit. Identify patterns in their choices: favorite techniques, colors, subjects, approaches. Introduce vocabulary: STYLE (distinctive gesture), PERSONNEL (point to self), DÉVELOPPER (growth motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Student artwork portfolios from unit, examples of distinctive artistic styles, style development timeline concepts
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle to see patterns in their work: help them identify specific preferences. If they clearly see their style: encourage articulation and development.

activities: Style Analysis (~8 min): Examine own artwork collection. Identify: favorite techniques, recurring themes, preferred colors, typical compositions. Practice vocabulary: 'Mon style personnel inclut...'
Intentional Style Development (~12 min): Create new artwork that deliberately emphasizes identified personal style elements. Make conscious choices to strengthen distinctive approach.
Style Articulation (~7 min): Write or record description of personal artistic style using advanced vocabulary. Practice explaining: 'Je développe mon style en...' Share style statements.
materials: Student artwork portfolios from entire unit
Art creation materials matching individual preferences
action.visualSupport: Style analysis templates, examples of artist style statements, personal style development examples
action.decisionPoint: If students can't identify their style: help them through guided questioning. If they're very aware of their style: challenge them to push style boundaries.

consolidation.activity: Personal Style Gallery. Display newest artworks that emphasize individual styles. Students present style statements and point out style elements in their work. Celebrate artistic individuality.
consolidation.assessment: Can students identify elements of their personal artistic style? Do they use style vocabulary appropriately? Can they create artworks that intentionally reflect their style?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students are proud of their styles: encourage continued development. If they want to change styles: discuss how artists evolve over time.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Style study without creation: Analyze famous artists' styles, identify style elements in artwork reproduction, practice style vocabulary through analysis activities.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Recognizing that everyone has their own way of creating and expressing

lessons.title: Art conceptuel
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create artworks that express specific ideas or concepts

mindsOn.activity: Discuss difference between decorative art and conceptual art. Show examples of art that expresses ideas vs art that's purely visual. Introduce vocabulary: CONCEPT (thinking gesture), IDÉE (lightbulb gesture), EXPRIMER (expression gestures).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of conceptual vs decorative art, idea-to-art connection diagrams, expression gesture cards
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If conceptual thinking is too abstract: use concrete examples with obvious meanings. If students understand quickly: introduce more subtle conceptual art examples.

activities: Concept Selection (~7 min): Choose important idea to express through art: friendship, family, seasons, growth, etc. Practice vocabulary: 'Mon concept est...' 'Je veux exprimer...'
Technique-to-Concept Matching (~8 min): Decide which advanced techniques best express chosen concept. Plan intentional connections: 'J'utilise cette technique parce que...'
Conceptual Artwork Creation (~12 min): Create artwork that clearly expresses chosen concept using intentionally selected techniques. Focus on meaning-making rather than just appearance.
materials: All advanced technique materials from previous lessons
action.visualSupport: Concept-to-technique matching charts, idea development flowcharts, conceptual art process examples
action.decisionPoint: If concept-technique connections are unclear: provide more structured guidance and examples. If students make clear connections: encourage sophisticated conceptual thinking.

consolidation.activity: Conceptual Art Presentations. Students present artworks and explain concepts being expressed. Audience tries to 'read' concepts in artwork. Practice vocabulary: 'Cette œuvre exprime le concept de...'
consolidation.assessment: Can students connect artistic techniques to conceptual expression? Do they use conceptual vocabulary meaningfully? Can they create art that communicates specific ideas?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If concepts are clearly communicated: celebrate successful conceptual art-making. If concepts are unclear: work on stronger concept-technique connections.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Conceptual planning without creation: Develop concept-to-technique plans on paper, analyze conceptual artworks, practice conceptual vocabulary through planning exercises.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that art can express feelings, ideas, and messages

lessons.title: Critique d'art
lessons.oneGoal: Students will analyze and critique artworks using advanced vocabulary

mindsOn.activity: Introduce art criticism as learning tool, not just opinion sharing. Practice constructive criticism vs destructive criticism. Introduce vocabulary: CRITIQUE (analytical thinking gesture), ANALYSER (close examination motion), VOCABULAIRE (words/speaking gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of constructive vs destructive criticism, art criticism question templates, analytical vocabulary lists
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students confuse criticism with being mean: emphasize constructive, helpful analysis. If they understand distinction: introduce more sophisticated critical concepts.

activities: Vocabulary Development (~8 min): Learn advanced art vocabulary for criticism: composition, technique, expression, effectiveness, innovation. Practice using words in sentences about artwork.
Structured Art Analysis (~10 min): Use guided questions to analyze artwork: What techniques? How effective? What concepts? What could be strengthened? Practice 'analyser' vocabulary systematically.

Peer Critique Practice (~9 min): Give constructive critiques of classmates' work using advanced vocabulary. Focus on helpful suggestions and genuine appreciation. Practice respectful critical discussion.
action.visualSupport: Art criticism question posters, advanced vocabulary cards, examples of good critique language
action.decisionPoint: If critiques become too harsh: refocus on constructive elements. If students are too gentle: encourage more specific analytical observations.

consolidation.activity: Critique Reflection. Students reflect on criticism received and given. Discuss how critique helps artistic growth. Practice vocabulary: 'La critique m'aide à...' Plan how to use critique for improvement.
consolidation.assessment: Can students give constructive, specific critiques? Do they use advanced art vocabulary in analysis? Can they receive criticism constructively and use it for growth?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If critique skills are strong: introduce peer critique partnerships for ongoing work. If skills need development: continue structured critique practice.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Critique practice with reproductions: Practice critique skills using famous artworks or art reproductions, focusing on vocabulary development and analytical thinking.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Discussing movies, books, music - expressing opinions about creative works

lessons.title: Processus créatif
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand and document their own creative process

mindsOn.activity: Discuss how they created their best artwork: what steps, what decisions, what changes. Introduce vocabulary: PROCESSUS (step-by-step motion), CRÉATIF (creative thinking gesture), DOCUMENTER (recording/writing motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Creative process flowcharts, examples of documented art-making processes, process documentation tools
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle to identify their process: use specific recent artwork examples. If they're very aware: encourage detailed process analysis.

activities: Process Documentation Setup (~7 min): Choose method for documenting creative process: photos, written notes, voice recordings, video. Practice vocabulary: 'Je documente mon processus créatif en...'
Live Process Documentation (~15 min): Create new artwork while documenting every step of creative process. Record decisions, changes, problems, solutions. Focus on metacognitive awareness.
Process Analysis (~5 min): Review documented process. Identify patterns, successful strategies, areas for improvement. Practice vocabulary: 'Mon processus inclut...' 'Je remarque que...'
action.visualSupport: Process documentation example formats, metacognitive question prompts, creative process analysis charts
action.decisionPoint: If documentation interferes with creation: simplify documentation methods. If students love process awareness: encourage detailed creative process study.

consolidation.activity: Process Sharing. Students share insights about their creative processes. Compare different approaches. Discuss how understanding process helps improve art-making. Celebrate process diversity.
consolidation.assessment: Can students identify and document their creative process? Do they use process vocabulary appropriately? Can they analyze their own creative decision-making?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If process awareness is high: encourage ongoing process documentation. If students struggle with metacognition: provide more structured process analysis tools.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Process analysis without new creation: Analyze creative processes used in previous artworks, discuss creative decision-making, practice process vocabulary through reflection.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how they learn and create in all areas of life

lessons.title: Collaboration artistique avancée
lessons.oneGoal: Students will collaborate on complex artworks requiring advanced technical skills

mindsOn.activity: Discuss how professional artists collaborate: sharing expertise, dividing complex tasks, combining different strengths. Introduce vocabulary: COLLABORATION (working together gesture), AVANCÉ (sophisticated level gesture), TECHNIQUE (skillful demonstration).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of artistic collaborations, role division charts, advanced technique review from unit
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle with collaboration: review basic cooperation skills. If they collaborate well: focus on advanced collaboration strategies.

activities: Collaboration Planning (~8 min): Form groups based on complementary advanced skills. Plan complex artwork requiring multiple techniques. Assign roles based on individual strengths.

Advanced Collaborative Creation (~15 min): Work on complex collaborative artwork. Each person contributes specialized advanced techniques. Practice vocabulary: 'Nous collaborons en utilisant nos techniques avancées!'
Integration and Refinement (~4 min): Combine individual contributions into unified artwork. Make collaborative decisions about final adjustments. Practice advanced collaboration vocabulary.
materials: All advanced technique materials from unit
action.visualSupport: Collaboration strategy cards, advanced technique role charts, successful collaborative artwork examples
action.decisionPoint: If collaboration breaks down: provide more structure and clear role definitions. If collaboration flows well: allow creative expansion and complex problem-solving.

consolidation.activity: Collaborative Artwork Presentation. Groups present artworks and explain how different advanced techniques were contributed by different collaborators. Celebrate successful artistic teamwork.
consolidation.assessment: Can students contribute specialized skills to collaborative work? Do they use advanced collaboration vocabulary? Can they integrate individual contributions into unified artwork?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If collaborations are very successful: plan more advanced collaborative projects. If skills need development: focus on collaboration skill-building activities.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Collaboration planning without creation: Plan complex collaborative artworks on paper, assign roles, practice collaboration vocabulary through planning exercises.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Professional artists working together, family projects requiring different skills

lessons.title: Installation artistique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create large-scale installations using advanced techniques

mindsOn.activity: Experience difference between small artworks and large installations. Walk through or around large classroom arrangement. Introduce vocabulary: INSTALLATION (environmental gesture), ÉCHELLE (scale comparison), ESPACE (space-defining gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Photos of art installations, scale comparison examples, spatial relationship demonstrations
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If space is limited: focus on smaller-scale installation concepts. If space is ample: plan ambitious installation projects.

activities: Space Analysis (~7 min): Examine available installation space. Consider how viewers will move through and around installation. Plan spatial relationships. Practice 'espace' vocabulary.
Large-Scale Planning (~8 min): Plan installation that uses advanced techniques at large scale. Consider how techniques work differently at installation échelle. Practice scaling vocabulary.
Installation Creation (~12 min): Execute installation using advanced techniques from unit. Work individually or collaboratively. Focus on spatial relationships and viewer experience.
action.visualSupport: Installation planning templates, scale relationship charts, spatial design examples
action.decisionPoint: If installation is too ambitious: scale down to manageable size. If students handle large scale well: encourage environmental and immersive elements.

consolidation.activity: Installation Experience. Walk through completed installation as viewers. Discuss how large scale and spatial relationships affect artistic experience. Practice installation vocabulary.
consolidation.assessment: Can students work effectively at large scale? Do they understand spatial relationships in installation? Can they adapt advanced techniques to installation échelle?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If installation is very successful: plan documentation and possible permanent display. If scale was challenging: focus on smaller-scale spatial relationship work.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Installation planning and analysis: Plan installations on paper or in miniature, analyze famous installations, practice installation vocabulary through planning exercises.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Museum installations, public art, themed room decoration

lessons.title: Maîtrise technique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate mastery of chosen advanced techniques

mindsOn.activity: Review all advanced techniques learned in unit. Students identify which techniques they feel most confident using. Introduce vocabulary: MAÎTRISE (mastery demonstration), DÉMONTRER (showing/proving gesture), CHOISI (choice-making gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Unit technique review poster, mastery examples, technique confidence self-assessment tools
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle to identify mastery: help them through guided reflection. If they're very confident: challenge them to demonstrate teaching-level mastery.

activities: Mastery Selection (~5 min): Choose 1-2 advanced techniques to demonstrate at mastery level. Consider personal strengths and interests. Practice vocabulary: 'J'ai choisi de démontrer ma maîtrise de...'
Mastery Artwork Creation (~18 min): Create artwork that showcases highest level of technical skill in chosen techniques. Focus on excellence, refinement, and personal style integration.
Mastery Documentation (~4 min): Document mastery artwork with artist statement explaining technical choices and skill demonstration. Practice mastery vocabulary in written reflection.
materials: High-quality art materials for mastery work
action.visualSupport: Mastery criteria checklists, technical excellence examples, artist statement examples
action.decisionPoint: If students set mastery goals too low: encourage them to challenge themselves. If goals are unrealistic: help them set achievable mastery demonstrations.

consolidation.activity: Mastery Exhibition. Present mastery artworks with formal artist statements. Celebrate individual technical growth and achievement. Practice mastery vocabulary in formal presentation context.
consolidation.assessment: Can students demonstrate genuine mastery of chosen techniques? Do they use mastery vocabulary appropriately? Can they articulate their technical growth and achievements?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If mastery demonstrations are excellent: document for portfolios and continued development. If students want to continue: plan advanced technique extension opportunities.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Mastery planning and analysis: Plan mastery demonstrations on paper, analyze technical mastery in professional artworks, practice mastery vocabulary through self-assessment.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Showing what they've learned, like performing a piano piece or demonstrating sports skills

beginningSpeaker.description: Student uses 1-2 technique vocabulary words with support, attempts basic advanced techniques with significant help, shows interest in technical learning
indicators: Shows willingness to try challenging technical work

developingSpeaker.description: Student uses 3-5 technique vocabulary words independently, executes some advanced techniques with minimal help, shows growing technical confidence

expandingSpeaker.description: Student uses 6+ technique vocabulary words in explanations, executes multiple advanced techniques independently, demonstrates technical problem-solving

bridgingSpeaker.description: Student uses sophisticated technique vocabulary naturally, masters advanced techniques and teaches others, shows artistic and technical leadership
indicators: Teaches and mentors other students in advanced techniques
